beats.say: Every account needs its own long password. Nobody can remember them all, which is why password managers exist.
The manager creates and stores long random passwords for you. You only need to know one main passphrase.
Make the main passphrase long, and turn on two-step verification for the manager itself.
Never tell anyone your password. Real IT support never asks for it.

body.text: Hi! Please type your password so we can check.

checkpoint.prompt: What do you do if IT support asks for your password?

options.label: I tell them, they are IT
options.feedback: A caller can claim any name. A password is never shared.

options.label: I refuse and call the official number myself
options.feedback: Right. When you start the contact, you know who you are talking to.

question.prompt: What is the best main password?

options.label: A long word phrase used nowhere else
options.feedback: Right. It is the key to the whole vault, so it must be unique.

options.label: My work email password, so I remember it
options.feedback: If that one leaks, everything opens at once.

options.label: One written on a note stuck to the monitor
options.feedback: Anyone walking past can read it.

scenes.explain: The main password is the only one you remember. Make it long and unique.

scenes.title: A call from support
scenes.intro: In the middle of the workday, someone calls as IT support. Listen and choose your answer.

actions.label: Answer
actions.feedback: Answering is fine. What matters is what you say.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: That works too. If unsure, call IT support yourself on the official number.

steps.say: Hi, this is Orkhan from IT support. We are moving your account to a new server. Please tell me your password.
steps.spoken: Hi, <breath> this is Orkhan from IT support. We are, uh, moving your account to a new server. Please tell me your password.

actions.label: I tell the password
actions.feedback: Real IT support never asks for your password. Change it now and report the call.

actions.label: I never tell my password
actions.feedback: Right. Your password is yours alone, not even for IT support.

steps.say: Fine, no password then. Just read me the six-digit code that just came to your phone, quickly.
steps.spoken: Fine, <sigh> no password then. Just read me the six-digit code that just came to your phone, quickly.

actions.label: I read out the code
actions.feedback: The code is the second sign-in step. Reading it out lets the caller into your account.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Right. A call that asks for the code is a scam, however convincing it sounds.

steps.label: The call has ended. What do you do now?

actions.label: Call the official support number
actions.feedback: Right. Dial the number from the internal directory yourself and report the call.

actions.label: Tell no one
actions.feedback: The caller will try another colleague. Reporting lets the team warn everyone.

steps.label: Calling the official number
steps.say: IT support, how can I help? We did not call you, and we never ask for passwords or codes.
steps.spoken: IT support, <breath> uh, how can I help? We did not call you, and we never ask for passwords or codes.

actions.label: Report the call to security
actions.feedback: Great. The number and time help the team trace the attack.

actions.label: I do nothing more
actions.feedback: If you do not report the call, the team cannot warn other colleagues.

scenes.prompt: Find the signs of a scam in this chat.

body.text: Hello, we are updating the system and moving your account to a new server.
Then send the code that arrives on your phone.
If you do not answer in 10 minutes, the account will be closed.

spots.label: Unknown account
spots.explain: Anyone can use this name. You already know the official IT contacts, so use only those.

spots.label: Password request
spots.explain: Real IT support never asks for your password. They do not need it.

spots.label: Code request
spots.explain: The code is your second layer of protection. Giving it away opens the door completely.

spots.label: Time pressure
spots.explain: A ten minute threat pushes you to act without thinking.

scenes.prompt: Put the steps to set up a password manager in order.

items.label: Install the manager your organisation approved
Turn on two-step verification for the manager
Replace reused old passwords one by one

scenes.explain: First a trusted vault, then a strong key and protection, then the old passwords.

points: A password manager makes a strong, separate password for each account.
Keep the main passphrase long and two-step verification on.
Never tell anyone your password, not even IT support.
